claims.title: Erdos-Straus conjecture: 4/n as three unit fractions
claims.statement: For every integer n >= 2, the equation 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z has a solution in positive integers x <= y <= z. Verified computationally far beyond 10^14 via divisor-enumeration methods, but no proof covering all n is known.

axis_texts.semantic: Every reciprocal expansion of 4/n needs at most three terms.
axis_texts.mechanism: divisor structure of quadratic polynomials in n parametrizes all solutions
axis_texts.math_structure: egyptian fractions divisor counting congruence classes density arguments
axis_texts.problem_shape: universal existence statement reduced to checking finitely many residue patterns
axis_texts.failure: proofs cover density-1 subsets; exceptional residue classes resist all known methods

attack_notes.summary: Proved complete structural reduction (Theorem A + Lemmas 2.4/2.5): E-S for primes equivalent to explicit two-condition Diophantine forall-statement with no gap in the chain. Six exceptional residue classes identified exactly as the core not coverable by bounded-template unions (mod 3/7/15/35 classes minus 24 units). First fully-proven reduction chain in this DB.

claims.title: Lonely Runner Conjecture
claims.statement: Given k runners with distinct constant speeds on a unit-length circular track, each runner is at some time at distance at least 1/(k+1) from every other runner ('lonely'). Proved only for small k (k <= 7ish); general case open.

axis_texts.semantic: Among k runners on a circle someone eventually gets at least 1/(k+1) ahead of all others simultaneously.
axis_texts.mechanism: view of view graph chromatic number bounds; torus orbit equidistribution
axis_texts.math_structure: view obstructions chromatic numbers diophantine approximation torus flows
axis_texts.problem_shape: existential over continuous time reduced to finite speed-ratio structure
axis_texts.failure: chromatic lower bounds insufficient beyond small k; equidistribution gives no uniform rate

attack_notes.summary: New exact chain up to EQ* yields conditional theorem: C(8) holds for generic 8-speed sets under pair-decay. Unblocking lemma identified in THEORY.md.

claims.title: Singmaster's conjecture: bounded multiplicity in Pascal's triangle
claims.statement: There is a finite upper bound on how many times any integer > 1 can appear in Pascal's triangle. The maximum known multiplicity is 6 (entry 3003); extensive searches found nothing above it, but no proof.

axis_texts.semantic: No binomial coefficient value repeats more than boundedly often.
axis_texts.mechanism: equalities C(n,k)=C(m,l) define algebraic curves whose integral points are rare
axis_texts.math_structure: binomial coefficients diophantine equations algebraic curves effective bounds
axis_texts.problem_shape: global bound from point-counting on curves
axis_texts.failure: effective bounds from Faltings-type results are astronomically weak

claims.title: Lehmer's totient problem
claims.statement: No composite n satisfies phi(n) | (n-1). If such n exists it must be odd, squarefree, and have at least 15 distinct prime factors (bounds pushed by successive searches); none found.

axis_texts.semantic: Compositeness is witnessed by phi(n) failing to divide n-1.
axis_texts.mechanism: phi divisibility forces extremely constrained multiplicative structure
axis_texts.math_structure: totients carmichael-like structures sieving modular arithmetic
axis_texts.problem_shape: nonexistence via structural constraints plus finite search
axis_texts.failure: each added factor multiplies search space; constraints weaken as factor count grows

claims.title: Giuga's conjecture
claims.statement: A composite n with sum_{p|n} 1/p - prod_{p|n} 1/p being an integer would be a counterexample to Giuga's conjecture that no such n exists. Any counterexample must be a Carmichael number with p | (n/p - 1) for every prime factor; searches among Carmichael numbers found none.

axis_texts.semantic: Composite n cannot satisfy this harmonic-sum integrality condition.
axis_texts.mechanism: condition couples primality-like behavior with prime-factor reciprocals
axis_texts.math_structure: carmichael numbers agoh-giuga congruences harmonic sums sieving
axis_texts.problem_shape: nonexistence via rare structured intersection of two sparse classes
axis_texts.failure: candidate class unbounded; searches rely on Carmichael enumeration growth

claims.title: Graceful Tree Conjecture (Ringel-Kotzig)
claims.statement: Every tree with m edges admits a graceful labeling: injective vertex labels from {0,...,m} such that edge labels |difference| are all distinct (1..m). Open since 1967 despite intense effort; verified computationally for many tree families and small sizes; all trees up to moderate vertex counts admit labelings under heuristic search.

axis_texts.semantic: Every tree can be gracefully labeled.
axis_texts.mechanism: labeling constraints propagate along tree structure; constructive induction resists generalization
axis_texts.math_structure: graph labelings combinatorial search parity arguments bipartite structure
axis_texts.problem_shape: universal construction statement; induction over tree decompositions fails globally
axis_texts.failure: known constructions cover restricted families (caterpillars, symmetrical trees); general trees resist

attack_notes.summary: Three classical routes proved blocked (affine rigidity + budget pigeonhole kill composition; leaf-induction strengthening refuted at n=6, machine-checked). Minimal separating lemma stated in THEORY.md.
